gloss: get, acquire, buy; possess, own; (of God) make and own; reed, cane
summary: To get and so to have as one's own: to buy a field, a servant or a threshing floor at a price, to get wisdom and understanding, and, of Yahweh, to acquire his people, as a father who made them, and to be the owner of heaven and earth. What is gotten is מִקְנֶה, above all livestock, a herdsman's wealth; מִקְנָה, a purchase, a slave bought with silver or a field with its deed; and קִנְיָן, property, or, of Yahweh, the creatures that fill the earth. The noun קָנֶה, reed or cane, the stalk, the staff, the sweet cane, the measuring reed of six cubits and the branches of the lampstand, is a separate word in every cognate language, and its tie to “acquire” is not known. Akkadian, Ugaritic, Aramaic, Arabic, Ge'ez and South Arabian share the verb qny “acquire, possess”, and Ugaritic also “create”.

words.gloss: get, acquire, buy; possess, own; (of God) acquire as his own, make; (niphal) be bought; (hiphil) make one a bondman
words.summary: About eighty-five times, nearly all qal. Its core is getting something so that it becomes one's own; most often by paying for it (with silver, at a price, from someone), and its opposite is מָכַר “sell”. The brief also files under this word the place Kanah (Jos 16:8; 17:9) and the reed of Ezk 40:5, and under the reed's key the twelve imperatives קְנֵה; each is given to its own word here. Ezk 8:3 הַמַּקְנֶה, “which provokes jealousy”, is the hiphil of קנא, not this verb.

stems.gloss: buy; get, acquire; acquire as one's own; possess, own

senses.definition: To get land, a servant, goods or materials by paying for them; the buyer (קֹנֶה) is set against the seller (מוֹכֵר).

evidence.note: “Buy us and our land for bread, and we and our land will be servants to Pharaoh.”
“Joseph bought all the land of Egypt for Pharaoh, for the Egyptians sold (מָכְרוּ) each his field.”
“I bought (וָאֶקְנֶה) the field from Hanamel … and weighed out to him the silver, seventeen shekels.”
“I will surely buy it from you at a price (בִּמְחִיר); I will not offer to Yahweh my God burnt offerings that cost me nothing.” So David bought the threshing floor.
“If you sell (תִמְכְּרוּ) to your neighbour or buy (קָנֹה) from your neighbour's hand, do not wrong one another.”
What was sold stays “in the hand of the one who bought it” until the jubilee.
In the jubilee the field returns “to the one from whom he bought it”, whose possession (אֲחֻזַּת) the land is.
“Let not the buyer (הַקּוֹנֶה) rejoice, nor the seller (וְהַמּוֹכֵר) mourn, for wrath is on all its multitude.”
“As the buyer, so the seller.”
“You will sell yourselves there to your enemies as servants … and no one will buy (וְאֵין קֹנֶה).”
The field Abraham bought from the sons of Heth, the burial place of Abraham and Sarah.
Jacob bought the portion of the field at Shechem for a hundred qesitah.
Joseph's bones buried in the field Jacob bought.
Potiphar bought Joseph from the Ishmaelites.
“If you buy a Hebrew servant, he shall serve six years.”
A soul the priest buys, “the purchase (קִנְיַן) of his silver”, may eat the holy things.
“To buy the poor for silver and the needy for a pair of sandals.”
“We have bought back our brothers the Jews who were sold to the nations.”
Omri bought the hill of Samaria from Shemer for two talents of silver.
To buy timber and hewn stone to repair the house of Yahweh.
“‘Bad, bad,’ says the buyer, and when he goes away he boasts.”
“Go and buy yourself a linen waistband.”
“Go and buy a potter's earthen flask.”
“Buy my field … for the right of redemption is yours to buy it.”
Boaz to the kinsman: “Buy it before those sitting here … on the day you buy the field from the hand of Naomi you buy also Ruth the Moabite.”
“I have bought all that was Elimelech's.”
“You have not bought me sweet cane (קָנֶה) with silver”: the verb and the reed side by side.
“Whose buyers slay them and are not held guilty.”

senses.definition: To gain something and make it one's own without a price paid in silver: above all wisdom, understanding, truth and instruction, which are worth more than gold and are to be bought and never sold; also a wife, servants, or, in Eve's word, a son.

evidence.note: “Get wisdom (קְנֵה חָכְמָה), get understanding; do not forget.”
“The beginning of wisdom: get wisdom, and with all your getting (קִנְיָנְךָ) get understanding.”
“How much better to get wisdom than gold, and to get understanding is to be chosen above silver.”
“Buy truth and do not sell (תִּמְכֹּר) it, wisdom and instruction and understanding.”
“Why is there a price in the hand of a fool to get wisdom, when he has no heart?”
“A man of understanding will get counsel.”
“He who listens to reproof gets a heart.”
“The heart of the discerning gets knowledge.”
“He who gets a heart loves his own soul.”
“Ruth the Moabite … I have acquired to be my wife, to raise up the name of the dead on his inheritance.”
“I acquired male and female servants.”
“We did not acquire any land.”
Eve, at Cain's birth: “I have gotten (קָנִיתִי) a man with Yahweh.”

senses.gloss: acquire as his own (Yahweh, of his people and land)
senses.definition: Of Yahweh: to make Israel, and the mountain of his holiness, his own possession, by bringing them out and redeeming them; said with גָּאַל “redeem”, and of a father who made and established his people. Isaiah uses it of the remnant he will acquire “a second time”.

evidence.note: “Until your people pass over, Yahweh, until the people pass over whom you have acquired (קָנִיתָ)”, after “the people whom you redeemed (גָּאָלְתָּ)” (Exo 15:13).
“Remember your congregation which you acquired of old, which you redeemed (גָּאַלְתָּ), the tribe of your inheritance, Mount Zion.”
“Is he not your father who acquired you (קָּנֶךָ)? He made you (עָשְׂךָ) and established you.”
“He brought them to the border of his holiness, this mountain which his right hand acquired.”
“In that day the Lord will set his hand a second time to acquire (לִקְנוֹת) the remnant of his people, which remains from Assyria, from Egypt …”

senses.gloss: possess, own; (of God) the maker and owner
senses.definition: The participle קֹנֶה is the owner, as the ox knows its owner; God Most High is קֹנֵה שָׁמַיִם וָאָרֶץ, owner, and maker, of heaven and earth. Of Yahweh forming a man in the womb, and of wisdom which Yahweh had at the beginning of his way, the verb has the sense of making something one's own by bringing it into being, as Ugaritic qny “create”.

evidence.note: Melchizedek: “Blessed be Abram of God Most High, קֹנֵה שָׁמַיִם וָאָרֶץ.”
Abram: “I have raised my hand to Yahweh, God Most High, קֹנֵה שָׁמַיִם וָאָרֶץ.”
“The ox knows its owner (קֹנֵהוּ), and the donkey its master's (בְּעָלָיו) crib; Israel does not know.”
“For you formed (קָנִיתָ) my kidneys; you wove me in my mother's womb.”
Wisdom speaks: “Yahweh acquired me (קָנָנִי) at the beginning of his way, before his works of old.”
“Your father who acquired you, he made you and established you.”

senses.definition: Only in Jeremiah 32, of fields and houses that will again be bought in the land after the captivity: the promise Jeremiah's own purchase was a sign of.

evidence.note: “Houses and fields and vineyards will again be bought (יִקָּנוּ) in this land.”
“Fields will be bought in this land of which you say, It is desolate.”
“They will buy fields for silver and write deeds … for I will return their captivity.”

stems.gloss: make (one) a bondman, acquire as a servant

senses.definition: Once: the man who denies he is a prophet says he has worked the ground since his youth because a man made him his own, a bondservant. The Targum renders it with the Aramaic aphel of the same root.

evidence.note: “I am not a prophet; I am a man who works the ground, for a man הִקְנַנִי from my youth.”

evidence.locator: Gen.4.1, קָנִיתִי → ἐκτησάμην; Exo.15.16 → ἐκτήσω; Deu.32.6 → ἐκτήσατο; Psa.78.54 → ἐκτήσατο; κτάομαι renders קָנָה ×17, with its other forms about as often again

evidence.note: “Do not acquire (κτήσησθε) gold or silver or copper for your belts.”
“He acquired a field with the wages of unrighteousness.”
“You thought the gift of God could be acquired with money.”
“By your endurance you will gain (κτήσεσθε) your souls.”

evidence.locator: 1Ch.21.24, קָנֹה … אֶקְנֶה → ἀγοράζων … ἀγοράζω; 2Ch.34.11; Isa.24.2, קּוֹנֶה → ἀγοράζων

evidence.note: “You were bought (ἠγοράσθητε) with a price; so glorify God in your body”: the believer is God's possession as Israel was (Exo 15:16).
“You were slain, and bought (ἠγόρασας) us for God by your blood out of every tribe.”
False teachers “denying the master who bought them”.

parallels.note: Redeem: Yahweh acquires the people he redeems.
Make, with כּוֹנֵן “establish”: the father who acquired Israel made them.
Master, owner: the ox's owner and the donkey's master.

opposites.note: Sell: the buyer and the seller.

words.gloss: livestock, cattle; possessions (in flocks and herds)
words.summary: What one has gotten, and so a herdsman's wealth: flocks and herds, donkeys and camels together. “Possessions of flocks and possessions of herds” (Gen 26:14) shows the sense acquired, and Sabaean qny and Syriac qenyānā also go from possessions to livestock. Job 36:33 is obscure (“the cattle also, concerning what rises”) and is left uncited.

senses.definition: Animals owned and kept, small and large, the chief wealth of the patriarchs and of the tribes east of Jordan; bought and sold, plundered and struck by plague.

evidence.note: “Abram was very heavy in livestock, in silver and in gold.”
Isaac “had possessions of flocks (מִקְנֵה־צֹאן) and possessions of herds (וּמִקְנֵה בָקָר)”.
“Give your livestock, and I will give you bread for your livestock … the livestock of the cattle are my lord's.”
Jabal, “the father of those who dwell in tents and have livestock”.
Jacob drove “all his livestock and all his property (רְכֻשׁוֹ) which he had gathered, the livestock of his acquiring (מִקְנֵה קִנְיָנוֹ)”.
“The men are shepherds, for they have been men of livestock.”
“The hand of Yahweh will be on your livestock in the field, on the horses, the donkeys, the camels, the herd and the flock.”
“All the livestock of Egypt died, but of the livestock of the sons of Israel not one died.”
Reuben and Gad had very much livestock, and Gilead was “a place for livestock”.
“You shall drink, you and your livestock and your beasts.”
Job's livestock: seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels.
“His livestock has spread out in the land.”
“I had great possessions of herd and flock (מִקְנֵה בָקָר וָצֹאן).”
Hezekiah had “possessions of flock and herd in abundance”.
“He gave over their livestock to flames.”
Gog comes against “a people gathered from the nations, who have gotten livestock and goods (מִקְנֶה וְקִנְיָן)”, to take them as spoil.

evidence.locator: Gen.13.2, מִקְנֶה → κτήνεσιν; κτῆνος renders מִקְנֶה ×20

evidence.note: The Samaritan set him “on his own beast”.
Among Babylon's merchandise, “cattle (κτήνη) and sheep”.

words.gloss: reed, cane; stalk; reed-staff; sweet cane; measuring reed; beam of a scale; branch of the lampstand; upper arm
words.summary: The reed of the Nile and the marsh, and things made of it or shaped like it: a hollow, jointed stem. Its cognates (Akkadian qanû, Ugaritic qn, Punic qn, Aramaic and Syriac qanyā) are all “reed” and never “acquire”, and Wiktionary traces the West Semitic forms to Akkadian qanû; the link to the verb is not known. The brief lists 74 tokens under this key: the twelve imperatives קְנֵה are the verb's, filed here by spelling.

senses.definition: The tall water plant of rivers and marshes, swaying and easily broken: a picture of weakness and of what is shaken.

evidence.note: The Nile's channels dry up, “reed and rush (וָסוּף) wither”.
“In the haunt of jackals, grass with reed and rush.”
Behemoth lies “in the covert of reed and marsh”.
“Yahweh will strike Israel as the reed is shaken in the water.”
“Rebuke the beast of the reed”, Egypt among its reeds.
Of Yahweh's servant: “A bruised reed (קָנֶה רָצוּץ) he will not break, and a dimly burning wick he will not quench.”
Isa 42:3 fulfilled in Jesus: “A bruised reed he will not break.”
“What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken by the wind?”, as 1Ki 14:15.

senses.definition: The stem bearing the ears of grain.

evidence.note: “Seven ears of grain came up on one stalk, fat and good.”

senses.definition: A staff of reed that splinters under the hand of one who leans on it: Egypt as Israel's false support.

evidence.note: “You trust in the staff of this bruised reed, Egypt, on which if a man leans it will go into his hand and pierce it.”
“Because they have been a staff of reed to the house of Israel.”

senses.definition: An aromatic cane brought from a far country, used in the holy anointing oil and as costly incense and merchandise.

evidence.note: In the holy anointing oil: “fragrant cane (וּקְנֵה־בֹשֶׂם), two hundred and fifty”.
“Why does frankincense come to me from Sheba, and sweet cane (וְקָנֶה הַטּוֹב) from a far land?”
Cassia and cane among the wares of Tyre.

senses.definition: A reed used as a measuring rod, and the length it measured: six long cubits, each a cubit and a handbreadth. With it the man in Ezekiel's vision measures the house.

evidence.note: “A cord of flax in his hand, and a measuring reed (וּקְנֵה הַמִּדָּה).”
“The measuring reed of six cubits, by the cubit and a handbreadth; and he measured the breadth … one reed, and the height one reed.”
“A full reed of six cubits.”
The outer wall, five hundred reeds on each side.
“A reed like a rod was given me: Rise and measure the temple of God.”
“A golden reed to measure the city.”

senses.definition: The balance on which silver is weighed.

evidence.note: “They lavish gold from the bag and weigh silver on the scale (בַּקָּנֶה), and hire a smith, and he makes it a god.”

senses.definition: The central shaft of the golden lampstand, and the six branches going out from its sides, three on each.

evidence.note: “Its base and its shaft (וְקָנָהּ).”
“Six branches (קָנִים) going out of its sides, three branches of the lampstand out of one side and three out of the other.”

senses.definition: Once, of the arm's bone, from which the arm could be broken: a jointed, hollow bone like a reed.

evidence.note: “Let my shoulder fall from its blade, and my arm be broken from its bone (מִקָּנָה).”

evidence.locator: Isa.42.3, קָנֶה → κάλαμον; Ezk.40.3, 5 → κάλαμος; Exo.30.23 → καλάμου

evidence.note: “A bruised reed (κάλαμον) he will not break”: Isa 42:3.
The measuring reed, as Ezk 40:3.
A reed put in Jesus' right hand in mockery.

greek.gloss: measuring rod; rule, standard; limit, sphere

evidence.note: “According to the measure of the rule (κανόνος) which God apportioned to us as a measure, to reach even to you”: the measured line of Paul's work.
“As many as walk by this rule (κανόνι), peace on them.”
“κάννα, Hebr. קָנֶה a cane, reed”: “a measuring rod, rule”.
“cf. κάννα, and Heb. קָנֶה, a reed”: “a rod or bar … a measuring rule … a rule or standard”.

words.gloss: purchase; one bought; purchase price; deed of purchase

senses.definition: A servant bought with silver from a foreigner, set beside the one born in the house; both were circumcised and could eat the Passover.

evidence.note: “One born in the house, or bought with silver (וּמִקְנַת־כֶּסֶף) from any foreigner who is not of your seed.”
“Every man's servant bought with silver (מִקְנַת־כָּסֶף), when you have circumcised him, may eat of it.”

senses.definition: Land gotten by buying, as against an inherited possession; and the sealed and open deeds that record it.

evidence.note: The field of Machpelah was made sure “to Abraham as a purchase (לְמִקְנָה)” before the sons of Heth.
“A field of his purchase, which is not of the field of his possession (אֲחֻזָּתוֹ).”
“I took the deed of the purchase (סֵפֶר הַמִּקְנָה), both the sealed and the open.”
“Put them in an earthen vessel, that they may last many days.”

senses.definition: What is paid to buy: in the jubilee laws, set by the years remaining.

evidence.note: “According to the many years you shall increase its price (מִקְנָתוֹ), and according to the few years you shall reduce its price.”
He repays his redemption “from the silver of his purchase”.

words.gloss: what is gotten: property, goods; (of Yahweh) his creatures

senses.definition: What one has gotten and owns, beside or including livestock; the getting itself (Pro 4:7).

evidence.note: “Their livestock and their property (וְקִנְיָנָם) and all their beasts, will they not be ours?”
Esau took “his livestock and all his beasts and all his property which he had gathered in the land of Canaan”.
The Levites' pasturelands, “for their livestock and for their property”.
“A soul, the purchase of his silver.”
Joseph made “ruler over all his possessions”.
“With all your getting get understanding.”
“Livestock and goods (מִקְנֶה וְקִנְיָן)”, the spoil Gog comes to take.

senses.definition: What Yahweh has made and owns: the living things that fill the earth.

evidence.note: “How many are your works, Yahweh! In wisdom you have made them all; the earth is full of your possessions (קִנְיָנֶךָ).”

words.gloss: acquire, get, possess; (ethpeel) be acquired; (aphel) cause to acquire, gain
words.summary: The Peshitta's ܩܢܐ (qnā), SEDRA lexeme 2837, for κτάομαι and its kin: the same verb as Hebrew קָנָה, with the Aramaic final א.

senses.definition: To get for oneself, by buying or by earning, and to have.

evidence.note: “Do not acquire (תֵּקנֻון) gold or silver or brass in your purses.”
“I tithe all that I acquire.”
“He acquired a field with the wages of sin.”
“With much money I acquired this citizenship.”
“Those who possessed lands or houses sold them.”
“By your endurance you will acquire your souls.”
“That each of you know how to possess his vessel in holiness and honour.”
Those who serve well “acquire for themselves a good standing”.

senses.definition: To be gotten, by a price.

evidence.note: “You thought the gift of God could be acquired (מֵתֿקַניָא) with the world's wealth.”

stems.gloss: cause to acquire, gain for one

senses.gloss: cause to acquire, gain for one
senses.definition: To bring one to possess something: faith that gains the soul, testing that gains endurance.

evidence.note: “We are of faith, which makes us acquire (דּמַקניָא) our soul.”
“The testing of your faith makes you acquire endurance.”

words.summary: The Peshitta's ܩܢܝܢܐ (qenyānā), SEDRA lexeme 2838: the same word as Hebrew קִנְיָן.

senses.definition: What one owns, which the disciple is to sell and leave, and share with a brother in need.

evidence.note: “Go, sell your possessions (קֵניָנָכֿ) and give to the poor … he went away sorrowful, for he had much property.”
“Whoever of you does not leave all his possessions cannot be my disciple.”
“Sell your possessions and give alms.”
The younger son's share, which he squandered.
“Those who had possessions sold them and divided to each as he had need.”
“Whoever has the possessions of the world and sees his brother in need …”
“God did not appoint us to wrath, but to the acquiring of life through our Lord Jesus the Messiah.”

words.summary: The Peshitta's ܩܢܝܐ (qanyā), SEDRA lexeme 2846: the same word as Hebrew קָנֶה, where the Greek has κάλαμος.

senses.definition: The reed shaken by the wind or bruised, the reed put in Jesus' hand and used to lift the sponge to him, the measuring reed of Revelation, and a reed pen.

evidence.note: “A bruised reed (קַניָא) he will not break”: Isa 42:3.
“A reed shaken by the wind?”
A reed in his right hand, and they struck him on the head with it.
“A reed was given me like a rod … measure the temple of God.”
“I do not wish to write to you with ink and pen.”

senses.definition: Ezra is to buy bulls, rams and lambs with the money entrusted to him.

evidence.note: “channel, canal”; “spear, lance”; “From Aramaic קַנְיָא / ܩܢܝܐ (qanyā, ‘reed, cane, tube’), from Akkadian qanûm”.

doctrine.statement: Melchizedek blessed Abram by “God Most High, קֹנֵה of heaven and earth”, and Abram swore by Yahweh under the same title (Gen 14:19, 22): the one who owns heaven and earth because he made them. Moses asks Israel, “Is he not your father who acquired you? He made you and established you” (Deu 32:6); the psalmist says, “you formed (קָנִיתָ) my kidneys; you wove me in my mother's womb” (Psa 139:13); and “the earth is full of your possessions (קִנְיָנֶךָ)”, all made in wisdom (Psa 104:24). As “the ox knows its owner (קֹנֵהוּ)” (Isa 1:3), so Israel should have known Yahweh. From the verses: what God made is his, man included; he owns because he made, and the one he made owes him his knowledge and his life.

At the sea Moses sang of “the people whom you redeemed (גָּאָלְתָּ)” and “the people whom you acquired (קָנִיתָ)” (Exo 15:13, 16), and the psalmist prays, “Remember your congregation which you acquired of old, which you redeemed, the tribe of your inheritance” (Psa 74:2). Yahweh acquired Israel by bringing them out of Egypt, and so they were his. The apostles say the same of believers in Christ: “you were bought with a price; so glorify God in your body” (1Co 6:20); the Lamb was slain and “bought us for God by your blood out of every tribe” (Rev 5:9); and false teachers deny “the master who bought them” (2Pe 2:1). From the verses: those whom God has bought belong to him and not to themselves, and the price paid for them was the blood of his Son.

In Pro 8:22 wisdom says, “Yahweh acquired me (קָנָנִי) at the beginning of his way, before his works of old.” The speaker is wisdom, who “cries at the gates” as a woman (Pro 8:1–3; 1:20–21), and the same verb tells every hearer to “get wisdom, get understanding” (Pro 4:5, 7): wisdom is something possessed. “Yahweh by wisdom founded the earth” (Pro 3:19), and “in wisdom you have made them all” (Psa 104:24). So Pro 8 personifies Yahweh's own wisdom, his before anything was made, and by which he made all. The New Testament calls Christ “the wisdom of God” and says he “became to us wisdom from God” (1Co 1:24, 30), and it says the child Jesus “grew and became strong, filled with wisdom” and “increased in wisdom and stature” (Luk 2:40, 52). From the verses: the wisdom of Pro 8 is not a second person beside God existing before the world. It is God's wisdom, shown in a man, Jesus, who was born and grew in wisdom.

With Jerusalem under siege and the land being given to the Chaldeans, Yahweh told Jeremiah to buy his cousin's field at Anathoth, weigh the silver and seal the deed of purchase in an earthen jar “that they may last many days”, “for thus says Yahweh of armies, the God of Israel: houses and fields and vineyards will again be bought in this land” (Jer 32:9–15). Yahweh's answer to Jeremiah's doubt was that he would gather them from all the lands, bring them back to this place, “and plant them in this land in truth”, and “fields will be bought in this land … for I will return their captivity” (Jer 32:37, 41, 43–44). Isaiah says that in the day of the root of Jesse, whom the nations will seek, “the Lord will set his hand a second time to acquire the remnant of his people” from Assyria, Egypt and the coastlands, and will gather the outcasts of Israel “from the four corners of the earth” (Isa 11:10–12). Ezekiel sees the gathered people in the latter days dwelling in their land with “livestock and goods (מִקְנֶה וְקִנְיָן)”, when Gog comes from the far north to take them as spoil (Ezk 38:8, 12–13, 15–16). From the verses: the land promised to Abraham is a real land in which fields will be bought and held; Israel's return to it, a second gathering under the Messiah's reign, is yet to come in full, and the invasion from the north is against that regathered people.

note: Drafted 2026-11-18. Root key קנה. Words left out: קִנָּמוֹן cinnamon (s.cc.ag; Exo 30:23, Pro 7:17, Sng 4:14), a foreign word with consonants q-n-m-n and no tie to this root (Jastrow files it under קנם; Greek κιννάμωμον, Rev 18:13, comes from it): it needs its own entry. קְנַז Kenaz (s.cc.ad) and the gentilic קְנִזִּי Kenizzite (s.cc.ae) are root קנז, filed here by BDB's alphabetical order; no name entry written. The place קָנָה Kanah (s.cc.ac; the wadi, Jos 16:8, 17:9, and the town in Asher, Jos 19:28) is a place name; its six verb tokens are the verb's, filed there by spelling. Ezk 8:3 הַמַּקְנֶה is קנא “provoke jealousy”. Names written: elkanah (אֶלְקָנָה, a.dl.bw) and mikneiah (מִקְנֵיָהוּ, s.cb.ae). Cain (קַיִן, Gen 4:1) is named with Eve's word קָנִיתִי, but the name is root קין; not given a name entry here. Open questions: (1) Whether קָנֶה “reed” belongs to the root at all: every cognate language keeps reed and acquire apart (Akkadian qanû N and qanû V; Anderson–Moser SEM001045 and SEM000326), and Wiktionary derives the West Semitic reed word from Akkadian. No sound in a merged letter separates them (the root has none of ח ע ש ז צ); the final ה may stand for w in the reed (*qanaw-) against y in the verb (qny), not checked. (2) “Create” for the verb rests on Ugaritic qny (Wiktionary) and the Phoenician title of El “qn ʾrṣ” (Karatepe), which is not yet cited: find it in krahmalkov-2000 or DEAPS. Ge'ez is cited only through Anderson–Moser and Wiktionary; check dillmann-1865 or leslau-1987. Arabic: Lane's قنو is in the supplement and not available; Wiktionary's قِنّ “slave … one that is kept or acquired” may bear on מִקְנָה (the bought slave) and the hiphil, root uncertain. (3) Job 36:33 מִקְנֶה is obscure and uncited. (4) The Peshitta of Act 20:28 uses ܩܢܐ (“which he acquired with his blood”); not cited, as it needs the reading of “God” there and of “his blood” weighed. (5) κανών is entered as a loan on Thayer's and Abbott-Smith's etymology through κάννα; check that κάννα is Semitic before review.
